name: math-library-accuracy-at-1024-operand-pairs-under-fast-math
rationale: Each of 1024 threads writes 32 words for its (x, y), compiled with the default fast math (MSL Table 8.2; air.fast_<name>.f32 wherever a fast variant exists): (sin x, cos x, tan x, sincos's sine), (sincos's cosine, asin x, acos x, atan x), (atan2(y, x), sinh x, cosh x, tanh x), (asinh x, acosh x, atanh x, exp x), (exp2 x, exp10 x, log x, log2 x), (log10 x, pow(x, y), powr(x, y), sqrt x), (rsqrt x, fmod(x, y), sinpi x, cospi x), and (tanpi x, x / y, atan2(x, y), y). Operands, 1,024 (x, y) float pairs in eight sections: 32 special pairs (both zeros, the smallest and largest denormals, the smallest normal, +-1, +-0.5, +-2, both infinities, a NaN, both largest finites, +-pi, +-pi/2, the neighbours of 1, Metal's fast trig flush point float(pi/2) * 2^22 and its neighbour, the exp limits); 192 in [-1, 1] (uniform, the eight floats below each of +-1, the powers 2^-1 to 2^-24, small magnitudes down to 2^-126); 128 at the float nearest k * pi/2 and its two neighbours for k = 1 to 32, and at 32 large k up to 2^126; 256 log-uniform over every binade from 2^-126 to 2^127, alternating signs; 128 in [0.5, 2] and at the 16 floats on each side of 1 and 1 +- 2^-k; 96 at the exponentials' edges and over [-104, 89]; 64 over the hyperbolics' ranges ([-20, 20], [-90, 90], [1, 1e30]); 64 pow pairs (wide exponents, results at the range's edges, exact powers and roots); and 64 trig arguments in [-1e4, 1e4] and at the flush point's neighbours and powers of two. y is an exponent, a divisor, or atan2's other operand, by section. Inputs generated deterministically (seed 0x7A4E297). Question (WP-TRN, DESIGN D297): for each function, how far Metal's answer and each device's are from the exact value, against Apple's stated bound, and what Metal answers where Apple states none.

name: fixed-array-eight-simdgroup-maximum

name: half-conversion-by-texture-buffer-reads
rationale: How Metal converts a texture buffer's texels to half when a half texture buffer reads them (the other half-conversion cases read 1D, 2D, array, 3D, and cube textures). Four 256-element half texture buffers: rgba32_float values around half rounding boundaries (ties, near ties, the overflow edge, subnormals, signed zeros, infinities, NaN, random), rgba8_unorm and rgba8_snorm with every code per channel, and rgba16_float halves of every binade with specials. Lane i reads element i of each and writes the four results widened to float to out[4i..4i+3] of buffer 0, pre-filled with 0xAB. The AIR has no loop.

name: linked-k48-quantized-matrix-multiply-half-64-non-transposed
rationale: Reaching variant of the zero-K case of this entry (DESIGN D296; WP-EVG, TODO 6.2), whose K = 0 stops the kernel before its arithmetic. One threadgroup of 128 lanes (4 simdgroups) runs the single 64x64 output tile: B = 1, M = N = 64, K = 48, so the tile is full in M and N (the unsafe loader path) and K runs one whole 32-deep block and a 16-deep remainder (the safe loader). The user constant keeps 8-bit unsigned weights, group size one, no bias, the non-cooperative loader; constant 122 binds a two-entry table (1 source, 1 destination). x is [M][K] (x_ld = 48) and every row holds 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 repeating, so every row of the result is the same: the linked destination callback, which writes table entry 1 at the column coordinate only, stores one value per column from every row, the same value, so the 64 words observed (offset 0, 256 bytes) do not depend on write order. W[k][n] (row stride w_ld = 64 bytes) holds q(n, k) = (11n + 3k + floor(3nk/5)) mod 16, nonlinear in n, so the column sums differ (63 of the 64 distinct whichever scale element the layout reads) and a column computed from another column's weights changes its word; scales and biases (scales_ld = biases_ld = 1, sized N*K) repeat 0.5, 1, 2 and 0, 1, 2, 3 (biases unread without the bias bit). Each dequantized weight is q * s, a multiple of 0.5 at most 30, exact in half and in the threadgroup tile; each product with x is a multiple of 0.5 at most 150 and each sum of 48 at most 7200, below 2^13: exact in float in any order or contraction, and on the half inputs.

name: sample-a-cube-face-and-a-1d-array-slice
rationale: Seven uncovered texture families in one kernel -- air.sample_texture_1d_array.v4f32 (6 corpus sources), air.write_texture_3d.i16.u.v4i16 (4), air.write_texture_1d.i16.v4f32 (4), air.sample_depth_cube.f32 (4), air.get_num_mip_levels_depth_cube (4), air.get_num_mip_levels_depth_2d (4) and air.write_texture_3d.i16.v4f16 (3). The four threads each write a different voxel of the two 3D textures and a different texel of the 1D one, with values derived from the thread index, so the writes pin their coordinate arithmetic against each other instead of all landing on texel zero; the ushort coordinates are the .i16 in those symbols. Both samples use a NEAREST sampler: the 1D array is sampled exactly on a texel centre so its result is a stored value and pins both the slice and the index, and every texel of a given cube FACE holds the same value so the depth cube pins face selection without also depending on the intra-face texel convention. This case compares the sample and query buffer: the two sampled values and the two mip counts, which must both be 1 for the single-level textures the manifest can express, in adjacent words so a lowering that returned zero or a size cannot match.

name: read-back-a-texel-written-past-a-texture-and-a-texture-buffer
rationale: Eight threads (DESIGN D250, D236.11's same-invocation forwarding; the texture and texel buffer forms, whose results Metal defines: a write out of bounds is ignored and a read out of bounds returns zero, so the case compares with Metal). img is a 4x2 r32_uint read_write texture holding 0xE1000000 + (4y + x); tb is an 8-texel r32_uint read_write texture buffer holding 0xF1000000 + i. Thread t writes 0xB0000000 | t to img at texel idx[t] (x | y << 16) and reads img at texel idx[8 + t] into out[2t], then writes 0xC0000000 | t to tb at element idx[16 + t] and reads tb at element idx[24 + t] into out[2t + 1]. Threads 0 to 3 write and read back one location past each resource: img (4,0), (0,2), (65535,1), (7,9) and tb elements 8, 9, 100, 1000; Vulkan's robustness may return the value the thread stored there unless the load is volatile, and Metal reads zero. Threads 4 to 7 write img's row 0 and tb elements 0 to 3, which no thread reads, and read img's row 1 and tb elements 4 to 7, which no thread writes, so every output is defined without a fence. The output is out: zeros for threads 0 to 3, then img (t-4, 1) and tb element t for threads 4 to 7.

name: gather-mm-rhs-nn-bfloat-k40-two-experts
rationale: Reaching variant of the zero-shape case of this entry (TODO 6.2, WP-RVC), whose zero extents stop the kernel before its arithmetic. One threadgroup of 64 lanes (2 simdgroups) runs the single 16x64 output tile: B = 1, M = 16, N = 64, K = 40 (gemm_k_iterations_aligned = 2, remainder 8), M and N aligned (user constant 3): the two whole 16-deep blocks go through the unguarded loader and the 8-deep remainder through the guarded one; constant 122 binds a two-entry table. The indices select expert 0 for rows below 8 and expert 1 for the rest, so the kernel walks two row segments, each a full tile multiply over its expert (experts_stride_b = N*K = 2560), writing only its own rows. B[e][k][n] (ldb = 64): expert 0 holds q(n, k) = (11n + 3k + floor(3nk/5)) mod 16, nonlinear in n, so the 64 column sums differ, and expert 1 holds q/2. A[m][k] (lda = 40): rows of segment 0 hold a = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 repeating along k, rows of segment 1 hold 2a, so every row of the result is the same (2a . q/2 = a . q): the linked destination callback, which writes table entry 1 at the column coordinate only, stores one value per column from every row, the same value, so the 64 words observed (256 bytes) do not depend on write order, and a row given the other segment's expert would write another. Every input is a multiple of 0.5 at most 15, exact in bfloat; every product is a multiple of 0.5 at most 75 and every sum of 40 at most 3000, below 2^12: exact in float in any order or contraction. Every loop is finite by these inputs: the row-segment scan stops at M = 16, the K loop runs gemm_k_iterations_aligned = 2 times, the segment loop ends after the two segments, and the element loops have constant trip counts.

name: float-to-bool-at-every-special-value
rationale: What air.convert from a float to i1 computes. L1d waits on it (BUILD_PLAN WP-L1d item 2: implement only from cited semantics; D52.3 refuses it NotImplemented; 96 local corpus sources call air.convert.u.i1.f.f32 or .f16). The front end emits it for bool(x), static_cast<bool>(x), (bool)x, and the condition of x ? a : b when x is a float. A half scalar is widened by fpext and converted as a float, which is the corpus's form; a vector keeps its lanes (air.convert.u.v4i1.f.v4f32, air.convert.u.v4i1.f.v4f16). Inputs: 40 float patterns and 40 half patterns, 4 per thread: signed zeros, the smallest and largest denormals of each sign, the smallest normals, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1 - ulp, 1, 1 + ulp, 1.5, 2, 3, -0.5, -1, -2, -3, 255, 256, large values (2^31, +-2^32, and 1e30 for float; 2^11, +-2^15, 65472, and 65504 for half), the largest finite of each sign, infinities, quiet and signalling NaNs of each sign, an all-ones NaN, and +-0.1. Output word i: bits 0-3 are the scalar float conversions of float lanes 4i..4i+3; bits 4-7 the same lanes through the vector float symbol; bits 8-11 the scalar conversions of the half lanes (fpext, then air.convert.u.i1.f.f32); bits 12-15 the vector half symbol; bits 16-31 are 0. What the readings would show: C++'s x != 0 answers 1 on every lane but the zeros, including 0.5 and the NaNs, and the denormals unless Metal flushes them (the module records air.compile.denorms_disable). A conversion to an unsigned integer truncated to one bit answers 0 for 0.25..0.75, 2 and 256, and 1 for 1, 1.5, 3 and 255. A saturating conversion answers 1 for every value >= 1 and 0 below it. The four groups agree lane for lane if the scalar and vector symbols and both widths name one function. The module is compiled with the default fast math, like the corpus rows (the calls carry no fast-math flags either way); float-to-bool-at-every-special-value-without-fast-math is the same program compiled -fno-fast-math.

name: depth-cube-and-cube-array-reads-at-32-and-16-bit-coordinates
rationale: air.read_depth_cube and air.read_depth_cube_array at 32- and 16-bit coordinates, decoded since D283. Texture 0 a depth cube depth32_float 3 x 3, texture 1 a depth cube array depth32_float 3 x 3 with 2 cubes, both read textures, every depth a distinct float in (0, 1) over many binades. Lane i reads face i mod 6 at texel ((i / 6) mod 3, (i / 18) mod 3) of texture 0, and of cube (i / 54) mod 2 of texture 1, each at 32- and 16-bit coordinates, and writes the four depths' words to out[i] of buffer 0 (uint4 elements), pre-filled with 0xAB. 128 lanes, so every texel of both textures is read; every coordinate is inside. The AIR has no loop.

name: fragment-custom-imageblock-depth

name: reduce-one-four-by-sixteen-tile-across-a-quad
rationale: M=N=4 and K=16 make the tile exactly one pass of every loop, so the four threads of one quad are the only lanes and each owns four of the sixteen k values. Every A entry is a power of two placed in exactly one lane's chunk, and B is all ones, so each row's answer names the lanes that reached it: 15 needs all four, 16 only lane 0, 32 only lane 3, and 192 lanes 1 and 2. alpha is one and beta is zero, so C never loads and the stored float4 is the quad reduction alone. Every sum is exact in binary32 in any association order.

name: an-8x8-simdgroup-matrix-filled-with-a-runtime-value

Every one of the 128 floats is 2.75, whichever cells a lane holds; every selected byte differs from the 0xab fill. The AIR has no loop.
